item.title: Erik Spoelstra Shrugs Off Doc Rivers’ Critique of Giannis Antetokounmpo
item.description: Miami Heat Head Coach Erik Spoelstra motions to his team during the first quarter during the play-in rounds between the Charlotte Hornets and the Miami Heat of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Spectrum Center. © Imagn On Thursday’s episode of “The Bill Simmons Podcast,” former Milwaukee Bucks coach Doc Rivers made some eyebrow-raising comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo. According to Rivers, Antetokounmpo is “a difficult guy” to coach, and his lack of “super IQ” on the basketball court curtails his athleticism and passing ability. This season, Antetokounmpo is under the tutelage of Erik Spoelstra as he suits up for the Miami Heat. In an interview with The Athletic’s Eric Nehm, Spoelstra acknowledged Rivers’ remarks. “Look, I like Doc, and I respect him, this is our business now. We went into the season thinking that that would be a process, playing with somebody (Giannis) that commands so much attention. That’s a different style than some of the guys that have come here, that have played before. We’ll be able to figure that all out.” Spoelstra, who is in his 19th season as the Heat’s coach, added that his team has responded well to his messaging. “We’ve already made a lot of strides. I’m on this mountaintop pounding my fist, and our guys understand it.” With Antetokounmpo in the fold, Miami dropped its first four games and now faces the difficult task of overcoming a 3-6 start. Integrating Antetokounmpo into the grand scheme of things has been a top priority for Spoelstra and his staff. Fortunately for the Heat, the team has plenty of time to learn how to maximize Antetokounmpo’s skill set this season. “He’s Not Wrong, But the Timing Is Wrong”: Analyst Reacts to Doc Rivers’ Comments on Giannis Antetokounmpo As for player-turned-analyst Antonio Daniels, Rivers isn’t necessarily wrong in his assessment of Giannis Antetokounmpo’s abilities. Appearing on SiriusXM NBA Radio on Friday, Daniels (a 14-year NBA pro who now works as a New Orleans Pelicans color analyst) broke down the nuances of Rivers’ comments. “He’s not wrong, but the timing is wrong…Because Doc Rivers is now retired from coaching and Giannis is no longer in Milwaukee. If this was said 3 or 4 years ago down the line, I get it.” Daniels added that the shortcomings Rivers pointed out don’t diminish Antetokounmpo’s “greatness,” arguing that it’s possible to be a great player while also being “difficult to play with.” READ MORE: “He Doesn’t Have a Super High IQ” – Doc Rivers Gets Honest About Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Biggest Weakness “My Gut’s Telling Me That” – Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Former Bucks Teammate Believes 2x MVP Could Reunite With Milwaukee in 2027 College Sports Network has you covered with the latest news, analysis, insights, and trending stories in college football , men’s college basketball , women’s college basketball , and college baseball !

item.title: Fans think Florida State hit new low as Boston College use ‘ring around the rosy’ tactic
item.description: Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images Even though they got the win against Boston College, one trick play from the Eagles embarrassed the Seminoles. Florida State managed to beat Boston College 31-24 in their first game without Mike Norvell, who was let go following their loss to Clemson. After absorbing a $50 million buyout to let Norvell go, fans of the Seminoles needed a big win. And even though the fans got their big win, one play did add another embarrassing moment to a season chock-full of them. Boston College’s ‘theatre kid antics’ get the best of Florida State During the third quarter of their game against the Florida State Seminoles, Boston College were at 2nd and Goal when they attempted a unique play. After a bizarre moving huddle, the Eagles pulled off a trick play with a fake handoff before Mason McKenzie made an underhand pass to Javarius Green for a touchdown. Understandably, many fans pointed out how bizarre it was to see this trick play, which was made famous by 1974’s hit movie, The Longest Yard, starring Burt Reynolds, who was also an alumnus of Florida State. One fan wrote: “No way the ‘ring around the rosy’ huddle worked.” However, a Seminoles fan shared a screenshot of the result and mocked Boston College: “Hope the theatre kid antics were worth it.” A third fan pointed out the history of the play in the NFL: “Didn’t Andy Reid do the same thing when he first got to KC?” A fourth fan loyal to Florida State paid little attention to the embarrassing play: “Norvell was fired, and change is coming. We’re good.” However, a fifth fan suggested the firing of Mike Norvell played a part: “When you fire your head coach, you’re not really expecting much out of the rest of the season.” And lastly, one final fan pointed out how absurd it was to criticise the Seminoles: “Boston College runs a weird play, then loses the game and somehow you think this is FSU hitting a new low?” Fans of the Seminoles will be hoping that this trick play will be the last of the embarrassing moments for them this season. item.title: Injury blow for Bangladesh! Shadman Islam ruled out of South Africa series after Sylhet Test setback
item.description: Bangladesh have suffered a major setback ahead of their upcoming Test tour of South Africa, with opener Shadman Islam ruled out after sustaining an ankle injury during the ongoing second Test against West Indies in Sylhet. The injury, which could involve both a tear and a fracture, has ruled the left-hander out of the two-match series, forcing the team management to look for an alternative at the top of the order. Shadman twisted his ankle on the second day of the Sylhet Test. A member of Bangladesh's selection panel confirmed his unavailability to Cricbuzz, revealing that the initial assessment indicated a tear, with the possibility of a fracture yet to be ruled out. Mahfizul Islam Robin in line for maiden Test call-up With Shadman unavailable, in-form Mymensingh opener Mahfizul Islam Robin is expected to earn a place in Bangladesh's squad for the South Africa tour. Cricbuzz understands that Robin is all set to be included in the Test squad. The opener is already in Sylhet with the Bangladesh team and has been working closely with the national coaching staff in the nets, preparing for a potential opportunity at the highest level. Meanwhile, Bangladesh are understood to be preparing to continue the ongoing second Test against West Indies with one batter short following Shadman's injury. Bangladesh's demanding South Africa schedule Bangladesh are scheduled to leave Dhaka on November 10 for their multi-format tour of South Africa, which will feature two Tests, three ODIs and three T20Is. The opening Test will be played at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg from November 15 to 19, while the second match is scheduled at SuperSport Park in Centurion from November 23 to 27.

item.description: Abbi Church (left) scored four tries against Fiji - she now has eight in four 2026 World Cup matches [Getty Images] Australia (8) 30 Tries: Church 4, Upton, Chapman Goals: Kelleher 3 Fiji (8) 14 Tries: Yaranamua, Paseka Goals: Yaranamua 3 Australia have reached their fifth successive Women's Rugby League World Cup final as they seek a fourth consecutive title - but they were made to work harder than anyone expected. They had breezed through the group stages and there looked to be little to stop the procession. But World Cup debutants Fiji had other ideas. For 40 minutes, one of the biggest surprises in the history of rugby league looked eminently possible. Order was eventually restored, thanks largely to four tries from Abbi Church, which set Australia on their way to a 30-14 victory. They will face old rivals New Zealand in the final next Sunday in Brisbane, kicking off at 05:10 GMT. But having given New Zealand a scare in their opening match before losing 18-12, Fiji came out at Sydney Football Stadium fully intent to unsettle and confront the red-hot tournament favourites. In doing so, they became the first side since New Zealand in the 2013 World Cup final to open the scoring in a game against Australia, who trailed for the first time at this tournament. "They're the games you want to play," Australia captain Isabelle Kelly said. "When you have those close games, it shows the character within the girls that are out there and in the battles. For me it was great to see everyone go back out there in the second half and stand up and do what we needed to do. "You have got to give full respect to the Fijians, they were incredible. We've been watching them closely over the World Cup and supporting them along the way. "What they've been able to do to come together to create such a special occasion for them, but also what they showcased out of the field was very good, very physical. They were amazing." item.title: Barcelona shot-stopper’s concerning numbers against Atletico Madrid ahead of La Liga clash
item.description: Barcelona shot-stopper’s concerning numbers against Atletico Madrid ahead of La Liga clash While Barcelona’s overall record against Atletico Madrid in recent years remains decent, the Catalans have fallen short against Diego Simeone’s men in high-stakes games in recent times. Last season, in particular, Barcelona suffered against Los Rojiblancos in both the UEFA Champions League and the Copa del Rey, with Atletico Madrid finding the right formula against their high line. Their defence, in that sense, struggled against Atletico Madrid on more than one occasion, leading to a couple of ugly scorelines for Joan Garcia who was Barcelona’s guardian in goal. A personal objective Barcelona have painful memories against Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) As reported by MARCA in a recent update, Atletico Madrid have managed to be Garcia’s biggest nightmare in recent times and their numbers against him speak volumes. Diego Simeone’s side, in that sense, is the Spanish goalkeeper’s worst opponent as they have scored a staggering ten goals against him over the years. Over his career so far, Garcoa has played against Atletico Madrid eight times – six times with Barcelona and twice with Espanyol. In that duration, he has conceded ten times – nine times with Barcelona and once for Espanyol. The 4-0 defeat in the semifinal of the Copa del Rey last season was the single-biggest culprit behind the star’s poor numbers against Los Rojiblancos , and he will be determined to turn it around tonight. Flick demands more A big test for Joan Garcia. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) While Hansi Flick’s side have been soaring in attack with an obnoxious goalscoring rate, their defensive numbers have not been as promising as the manager would have hoped. The Catalans have conceded twelve goals in eleven games so far in La Liga, and the coach is not satisfied with the team’s defensive numbers. Going up against Atletico Madrid , who boast of La Liga’s best defensive record with just eight goals conceded so far, the Blaugrana will be up for a massive challenge but also a big chance to prove their defensive superiority. All eyes, needless to say, will be on Joan Garcia to see if he can move past the ghosts of the past and put up a strong showing that helps the team to a commanding win. item.description: PALM BEACH GARDENS — Sometime after Lexi Thompson agreed to be a part of the fledgling WTGL, she found out that participation would be limited. Thompson, the Delray Beach resident and 11-time LPGA champion, announced in August her and her husband, Max Provost, were expecting their first child, a girl. She is due in February. Suddenly, the WTGL had company on Thompson's list of priorities. But the WTGL still is something the 31-year-old is passionate about, and will remain involved with through the first season even if she will not be hitting balls at the SoFi Center, into the world's largest simulator, until the season's end in late December. "If I play all the matches or if I just play one, just to be able to grow the game, that's what it's all about," said Thompson, who is playing for Detroit's Motor City Golf Club. If it's one, it will be at Motor City's debut Tuesday, Nov. 19. at 8 p.m., against Los Angeles Golf Club. LA was part of WTGL's unveiling Sunday against New York Golf Club. Thompson is part of Motor City's lineup along with Ronni Yin and Jeeno Thitikul. They will face LA's Michelle Wie West, Aki Iwai and Kiara Romero. Thompson will be about 25 weeks pregnant for the opener. Lexi Thompson prepared to adjust golf swing while pregnant Madelene Sagstrom was 27 weeks pregnant in June when she played the Dow Championship in Midland, Michigan. She finished tied for ninth with a 10-under 270. The previous week, at U.S. Women’s Open in June at Riviera, the 33-year-old Sagstrom missed the cut. Sagstrom was a crowd favorite, and receiving several ovations. Thompson was watching and marveled at how Sagstrom maintained her swing. "Her swing looked incredible," Thompson said at WTGL media day in September. "I'm sure it's difficult. It's something to plan around for sure. The next few months might be very challeging for me." Sagstrom called the adjustments necessary to swing a golf club while another human is growing inside your body ... "the most fun." She changed all her clubs and was constantly making adjustments putting. "Do I go a little bit more on top of the belly now or go around it?" she said. "You get away from that perfect golf, and just be a little bit more flexible." Thompson will find that out for at least one and perhaps more WTGL matches with Motor City's second match Nov. 16. Motor City's final two matches are Nov. 29 and Dec. 1. Whether she is on the floor of the SoFi Center or in the owner's box, Thompson will be supporting Motor City, and, for that matter, the other 24 women who comprise the five WTGL rosters. item.title: 91-Year-Old Athlete, Who Started Competing in Track and Field at 60, Is Still Breaking World Records: ‘Never Too Late’
item.description: Flo Meiler. Credit: aging untold NEED TO KNOW Florence Meiler started her track-and-field career 31 years ago Now 91, the Vermont athlete is breaking world records, including in the 2,000-meter steeplechase, 80-meter hurdles, pole vault, high jump, triple jump and pentathlon During motivational speeches, Meiler tells fellow senior citizens that it’s “never too late” to take up a sport or try new things Three decades ago, a then-60-year-old Florence Meiler was recruited by her best friend to try track and field . For 20 years, she and that friend, Barbara Jordan, trained and competed together, breaking world records at track-and-field events, as documented in an Oct. 30 Aging Untold talk show segment. But 10 years ago, their time as athletic partners was cut short when Jordan was diagnosed with cancer and forced to stop sports altogether. Then, in 2020, Jordan died at age 85 after a five-year cancer journey. Now 91, Meiler still thinks about her late best friend as she continues to break world records in her age group, 31 years after starting the sport. “I miss her so much,” the Shelburne, Vt., athlete told Aging Untold . In a 2020 video profile aired as part of the Olympic Channel’s Body+ series , Meiler elaborated on her longtime friendship. “Training together was fantastic because we would challenge each other and we would criticize each other,” the master athlete explained. Pole vaults on a track field. Credit: Isaiah Vazquez/NCAA Photos via Getty Meiler continued, “It’s really a struggle for me to train by myself. It is a real struggle, but I have a determination, and I put Barb into my mind, and I’ve got to do this for Barb and I’ve got to do this for the state of Vermont.” That determination has since led her to break several world records in her 90–94 age group. According to World Masters Athletics , Meiler holds world records for the 2,000-meter steeplechase (20:54.78), 80-meter hurdles (34.55), pole vault (1.30), high jump (0.92), triple jump (4.55) and pentathlon (2218). “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me.’ That’s a wonderful feeling,” she told Aging Untold . As for her motto, Meiler told the Olympic Channel it’s three simple words: “Never too late.” Read the original article on People

item.title: Sergio Garcia reveals what Luke Donald has already told him about the Ryder Cup ahead of Adare Manor
item.description: Photo by Ross Kinnaird/Getty Images Sergio Garcia is on the outside looking in when it comes to the European Ryder Cup set-up right now. The complete opposite is true for Rory McIlroy, who has played a key role for Team Europe in every event since 2010. And the golfing legacies of the Spaniard and the Northern Irishman have headed in completely different directions over the past few years. Garcia and McIlroy actually enjoyed many Ryder Cups together, notably the incredible win at Medinah in 2012 and the dominant wins in 2014 and 2018. Luke Donald is someone who the Spaniard was very close with as well before he joined LIV Golf in 2022. However, Garcia has not made the European Ryder Cup team since 2021, mostly due to the fact that he left the PGA Tour and DP World Tour to join LIV Golf back in 2022 The 46-year-old from Castellon is currently the highest points scorer in Ryder Cup history, and he will be desperate to add to his tally next year at Adare Manor. Sergio Garcia reveals what Luke Donald has already told him about the Ryder Cup With Garcia keen to rejoin the DP World Tour after his exit from LIV Golf, he may well be able to play his way back onto the Ryder Cup team. During an interview with Golf Magic , Garcia was asked whether he has spoken to Donald about his chances of making the team at Adare Manor next year. “I had a little chat with Luke in Ireland, mentioning that I was trying as hard as I could to make the team, and he said that he didn’t expect anything else, so that was nice,” revealed Garcia. “I also told him that obviously if I couldn’t be there as a player that I would love to help in any way possible.” Sergio Garcia was also asked whether he has spoken to any of the European players about a possible reintegration into the Ryder Cup setup. “I haven’t really talked to Rory [McIlroy] about it much, but I have talked to Justin Rose and a couple of others, and obviously they are on the same page,” Garcia replied. “If there is any way that I can help then they are happy for me to be there and that’s what I’m going to try to do. So we’ll see what the year brings us.” The onus is now on Sergio Garcia to play some exceptional golf over the next nine months or so in order to qualify automatically for the Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor. However, if he is unable to qualify, it’s highly unlikely that he will receive a captain’s pick, given how badly he has damaged some of his relationships within the game.

item.title: Is there a a €65 million problem waiting around the corner for Bayern Munich?
item.description: (Photo by Maciej Rogowski/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich might have a €65 million Dayot Upamecano problem, and nobody seems particularly interested in talking about it. For months, one of the biggest unspoken questions surrounding Bayern Munich has been whether Dayot Upamecano’s new contract would come with a relatively modest release clause that could make him vulnerable to an exit next summer. Now, the reported €65 million figure is back in the spotlight given how excellent the French center-back has been, and Bayern Munich board member for sport Max Eberl was given an opportunity to address it. Understandably, Eberl chose not to. When asked about the rumored release clause, the Bayern sporting director offered a carefully worded response. “I’m not here to discuss the details of the contract. One thing is clear: we’ve extended Upamecano’s contract, and we’re absolutely delighted that we di d. To be honest, he feels extremely comfortable here,” Eberl told Tz’s newsletter, Absolut Bayern (as capt ured by @iMiaSanMia ). That is certainly a nice sentiment, but it does not exactly answer the question. Nobody at Bayern Munich wants to entertain the possibility of losing Upamecano, particularly with the French international establishing himself as one of the best center-backs in world football. However, if the reported €65 million release clause is real, the club could have very little control over his future next summer if a major European club decides to activate it. Bayern Munich deserves credit for securing Upamecano’s ext ension, but the circumstances surrounding that deal remain an elephant in the room. Everyone seems happy to celebrate the renewal, and nobody seems particularly eager to discuss what happens if someone comes calling with €65 million.
